This function returns the path to one of them, so you can try out metadata import (and run the examples in this documentation) without supplying files of your own. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The file name of the example, such as `"define.xml"`. See the *Available Examples* section for the full list. An unknown name raises a `ValueError` that lists the valid names. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Path]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The path to the bundled file, which can be passed directly to `import_metadata()`. ::: ## Available Examples {.doc-available-examples} | Name | Format | Description | |------|--------|-------------| | `"define.xml"` | `cdisc_define` | Define-XML 2.0 document with the DM and AE domains | | `"sdtm_ct.xml"` | `cdisc_ct` | SDTM Controlled Terminology with common codelists | | `"datapackage.json"` | `frictionless` | Frictionless Data Package for a transactions table | | `"table_schema.json"` | `table_schema` | Frictionless Table Schema for sensor readings | | `"weather_csvw.json"` | `csvw` | W3C CSVW metadata for weather observations | | `"dm.xpt"` | `xpt` | SAS Transport file with a small SDTM Demographics dataset | The XML formats need the `lxml` package and the XPT file needs `pyreadstat`. The JSON formats don't need any extra packages. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Get the path to the bundled Define-XML document: ::: {#9c6f3c0c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb define_path = pb.load_metadata_example("define.xml") print(define_path.name) print(define_path.exists()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` define.xml True ``` ::: ::: The result is a `pathlib.Path` to a file inside the installed package. Pass it to [`import_metadata()`](`pointblank.import_metadata`) to read the metadata: ::: {#966d8e96 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} package = pb.import_metadata(define_path) for name in package.keys(): meta = package[name] print(f"{name}: {meta.dataset_label} ({len(meta)} variables)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` DM: Demographics (13 variables) AE: Adverse Events (10 variables) ``` ::: ::: The format was detected from the file's contents, and because the document describes two datasets the result is a [`MetadataPackage`](`pointblank.MetadataPackage`) with one entry per dataset. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~import_metadata`) : Read metadata from a file, such as one of these examples.
